# Write test cases from a story

Here, test cases are a document a tester reviews with Product before development starts. They are not automated tests. If the user asks for automated tests or test code, this skill doesn't apply.

## Who reads this, and why it matters

A tester and a product owner read this document together, line by line, in one meeting, before any code exists. The rules below follow from that.

- Aim for 2 to 5 cases per acceptance criterion. A review that runs past an hour loses the people it's for, so choose the cases most likely to find a bug: the boundaries, the time zone and daylight-saving edges, the empty state.
- When two cases differ only in their data, make them one case and list the data values in it. The reader learns nothing new from the second row.
- Give every open question a proposed answer. Product can accept or change a proposal in a minute; a bare question stalls the meeting.
- Work only from the story and the documents it links to, not `src/` or `tests/`. The code may be missing or wrong, and the test cases are there to check it, not to copy it.

## Steps

1. Read the story and every document it links to. If the story file doesn't exist or has no acceptance criteria, stop: say what you looked for and ask which story is meant. Don't invent one.
2. Write the cases to `docs/test-cases/<story-id>.md`. Create the folder if it doesn't exist.
3. Start the file with the test data you'll reuse: the user, their time zone, the dates and the "now" each case assumes.
4. Write one table per acceptance criterion, plus one for any non-functional requirement. Use the columns ID (`TC-<story number>-<n>`), Condition, Steps and Expected result. Give concrete data: dates, times and time zones.
5. Test both sides of every number in the story. For users, dates, daylight-saving days and journal notes, use the team's conventions in `references/test-data.md`: open it before you write the test data.
6. Every expected result must come from the story or the documents it links to. If they don't say, add an open question instead of guessing.
7. End the file with "Open questions" as a table: #, Question, Cases affected, Proposed answer, Who decides. Product owns the stories; Regulatory & Brand owns the claims register.
8. Check the document: `python3 /Users/you/ai-projects/video-generator-ai/courses/agent-skills-for-testers/lessons/10-skills-that-hand-off/material/copy-direct/.claude/skills/write-test-cases/scripts/check_cases.py docs/stories/<story-id>.md docs/test-cases/<story-id>.md`. Fix every FAIL and run it again until it passes. If a criterion really needs more than 5 cases, keep them and add a line under its heading: `More than 5: <reason>`.
9. Reply with the file path, the number of cases per acceptance criterion, the checker's last line, and the open questions.

## Example rows

| ID | Condition | Steps | Expected result |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-116-8 | A 00:15 bedtime counts for the previous date | 1. Log standard nights for 12 and 13 Nov. 2. Log a night with bed 00:15 on Sun 15 Nov, wake 07:45. 3. Now = Thu 19 Nov 10:00 Toronto. | The night is the night of Sat 14 Nov and is counted in the window. |

| # | Question | Cases affected | Proposed answer | Who decides |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A mean exactly halfway between two 5-minute steps (442.5 min): round up or down? | TC-116-29 | Round half up: 7 h 25 min. | Product |


ARGUMENTS: S-117

1	# S-117: Export the diary as CSV
2	
3	**As a** NightJar user,
4	**I want to** download my whole sleep diary as a CSV file,
5	**so I can** keep my own copy or move it to another app.
6	
7	| Field | Value |
8	|---|---|
9	| Traces to | [BR-07](../requirements/BR-07.md) |
10	| Status | Ready for development (no code yet) |
11	| Owner | Product (fictional: Priya N.) |

13	## Acceptance criteria
14	
15	- **AC1**: An "Export CSV" button on the home page downloads a file named
16	  `nightjar-diary-YYYY-MM-DD.csv`, using today's date in the user's current time zone.
17	- **AC2**: The file has a header row and the same columns as the import:
18	  `bedtime,wake_time,timezone,notes`.
19	- **AC3**: Times are ISO 8601 with the UTC offset that applied in that night's own time
20	  zone, for example `2026-03-01T00:25:00-05:00`.
21	- **AC4**: Nights are in "night of" order, oldest first.
22	- **AC5**: Journal notes are exported exactly as entered, including commas, quotes, line
23	  breaks and non-English text, using standard CSV quoting.
24	- **AC6**: Importing an exported file into an empty diary gives the same nights.
25	- **Edge**: An empty diary exports the header row only.
26	- **Non-functional**: Exporting 1,000 nights takes under 2 seconds.

# S-117: Export the diary as CSV

**As a** NightJar user,
**I want to** download my whole sleep diary as a CSV file,
**so I can** keep my own copy or move it to another app.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Traces to | [BR-07](../requirements/BR-07.md) |
| Status | Ready for development (no code yet) |
| Owner | Product (fictional: Priya N.) |

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1**: An "Export CSV" button on the home page downloads a file named
  `nightjar-diary-YYYY-MM-DD.csv`, using today's date in the user's current time zone.
- **AC2**: The file has a header row and the same columns as the import:
  `bedtime,wake_time,timezone,notes`.
- **AC3**: Times are ISO 8601 with the UTC offset that applied in that night's own time
  zone, for example `2026-03-01T00:25:00-05:00`.
- **AC4**: Nights are in "night of" order, oldest first.
- **AC5**: Journal notes are exported exactly as entered, including commas, quotes, line
  breaks and non-English text, using standard CSV quoting.
- **AC6**: Importing an exported file into an empty diary gives the same nights.
- **Edge**: An empty diary exports the header row only.
- **Non-functional**: Exporting 1,000 nights takes under 2 seconds.

1	# NightJar test data conventions
2	
3	Use these in every test-case document, so cases from different stories and different people use the same users, dates and data, and anyone can reproduce them.
4	
5	## Users
6	
7	| User | Time zone | Notes |
8	|---|---|---|
9	| Sam | America/Toronto | The default user. Quiet hours 23:00–07:00. |
10	| Lee | Europe/London | Use for London cases and zero UTC offset. |
11	| Ana | America/Toronto, then Europe/London | The traveller: changes time zone mid-week. |
12	
13	## The clock
14	
15	- Default "now": **Thu 19 Nov 2026 10:00, America/Toronto**. Say so at the top of the document and in any case that uses a different "now".
16	- Just before and after local midnight: Thu 19 Nov 23:59 and Fri 20 Nov 00:00 Toronto.
17	
18	## Daylight saving, 2026
19	
20	| Zone | Spring forward | Fall back |
21	|---|---|---|
22	| America/Toronto | Sun 8 Mar, 02:00 → 03:00 (EST −05:00 → EDT −04:00) | Sun 1 Nov, 02:00 → 01:00 (EDT → EST) |
23	| Europe/London | Sun 29 Mar, 01:00 → 02:00 (GMT +00:00 → BST +01:00) | Sun 25 Oct, 02:00 → 01:00 (BST → GMT) |
24	
25	A night that crosses a change is an hour shorter (spring) or longer (fall) than the clock suggests.
26	
27	## Standard nights
28	
29	- **Standard night:** bed 23:00, wake 06:30 local (7 h 30 min).
30	- **After-midnight night:** bed 00:25, wake 08:00. Its "night of" date is the day before.
31	
32	## Named data sets
33	
34	| Name | Contents |
35	|---|---|
36	| D-empty | No nights. |
37	| D-week | Sam's standard nights for the nights of 12 to 18 Nov 2026. |
38	| D-dst | One Toronto and one London night across each change above. |
39	| D-notes | One night for each tricky note below. |
40	| D-1000 | 1,000 standard nights for Sam, notes from D-notes repeated. |
41	
42	## Tricky journal notes
43	
44	Use these exact values, so a failure points to the same text every time.
45	
46	| # | Note | What it tests |
47	|---|---|---|
48	| N1 | `Slept well, woke once` | comma |
49	| N2 | `Felt "rested" today` | double quotes |
50	| N3 | `Late dinner` + line break + `then reading` | line break |
51	| N4 | `Très bien 😴` | non-English text and emoji |
52	| N5 | `  padded  ` (two spaces each side) | leading and trailing spaces |
53	| N6 | `=1+1` | a value a spreadsheet may run as a formula |
54	| N7 | 2,000 × `a` | very long text |
55	| N8 | (empty) | empty note |
56	
57	## Wording
58	
59	Any text the user sees must pass the claims check in `docs/claims.md`. Banned patterns include insomnia, sleep apnea, treat, cure, diagnose, anxiety disorder, prescribe and clinically proven.

# NightJar test data conventions

Use these in every test-case document, so cases from different stories and different people use the same users, dates and data, and anyone can reproduce them.

## Users

| User | Time zone | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Sam | America/Toronto | The default user. Quiet hours 23:00–07:00. |
| Lee | Europe/London | Use for London cases and zero UTC offset. |
| Ana | America/Toronto, then Europe/London | The traveller: changes time zone mid-week. |

## The clock

- Default "now": **Thu 19 Nov 2026 10:00, America/Toronto**. Say so at the top of the document and in any case that uses a different "now".
- Just before and after local midnight: Thu 19 Nov 23:59 and Fri 20 Nov 00:00 Toronto.

## Daylight saving, 2026

| Zone | Spring forward | Fall back |
|---|---|---|
| America/Toronto | Sun 8 Mar, 02:00 → 03:00 (EST −05:00 → EDT −04:00) | Sun 1 Nov, 02:00 → 01:00 (EDT → EST) |
| Europe/London | Sun 29 Mar, 01:00 → 02:00 (GMT +00:00 → BST +01:00) | Sun 25 Oct, 02:00 → 01:00 (BST → GMT) |

A night that crosses a change is an hour shorter (spring) or longer (fall) than the clock suggests.

## Standard nights

- **Standard night:** bed 23:00, wake 06:30 local (7 h 30 min).
- **After-midnight night:** bed 00:25, wake 08:00. Its "night of" date is the day before.

## Named data sets

| Name | Contents |
|---|---|
| D-empty | No nights. |
| D-week | Sam's standard nights for the nights of 12 to 18 Nov 2026. |
| D-dst | One Toronto and one London night across each change above. |
| D-notes | One night for each tricky note below. |
| D-1000 | 1,000 standard nights for Sam, notes from D-notes repeated. |

## Tricky journal notes

Use these exact values, so a failure points to the same text every time.

| # | Note | What it tests |
|---|---|---|
| N1 | `Slept well, woke once` | comma |
| N2 | `Felt "rested" today` | double quotes |
| N3 | `Late dinner` + line break + `then reading` | line break |
| N4 | `Très bien 😴` | non-English text and emoji |
| N5 | `  padded  ` (two spaces each side) | leading and trailing spaces |
| N6 | `=1+1` | a value a spreadsheet may run as a formula |
| N7 | 2,000 × `a` | very long text |
| N8 | (empty) | empty note |

## Wording

Any text the user sees must pass the claims check in `docs/claims.md`. Banned patterns include insomnia, sleep apnea, treat, cure, diagnose, anxiety disorder, prescribe and clinically proven.
